observations.text: SP flew the PAR final with the IP directing azimuth and elevation corrections throughout, as expected at this point of the syllabus. Altitude until on final reached 300 feet from the assigned value and the aircraft went 300 feet high on the glide path before IP direction restored the profile. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent response to the final controller's corrections is expected to improve on the next sortie.

SP, on the first GCA finals, responded to every azimuth and elevation correction issued by the final controller and needed only verbal prompts from the IP, with no control intervention required. Heading was held within 10 degrees of the corrected value, altitude until on final within 300 feet and airspeed within +20/-10 knots of final approach speed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the GCA approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual and Local Area Procedures, taking each controller correction without prompting from the IP. Minor errors appeared - up to 8 degrees of heading, 200 feet of altitude until on final and 15 knots above final approach speed - and all were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the PAR pattern and final accurately and promptly, applying the final controller's corrections as issued. Heading stayed within 5 degrees, altitude until on final within 150 feet, airspeed within +10/-5 knots, and the aircraft remained only slightly above or slightly below the glide path to decision height. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the GCA approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual, MAIP and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 with negligible deviations. Heading, altitude until on final and airspeed were held essentially on the assigned values, and the aircraft tracked the glide path with corrections so small that the final controller issued no repeat calls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a lagging power and attitude technique on the glide path, did not arrest the descent at the final controller's below glide path call, with the result that the aircraft went more than 150 feet low and the IP had to take the controls and re-establish the profile. Further practice of glide path control on PAR final is required.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the controller's transmissions, did not monitor airspeed on the PAR final, with the result that speed decayed 15 knots below final approach speed and the IP directed the power correction and flew part of the approach. Recognition of the deviation came only after IP input.

SP completed the GCA approach within the standard for this training block, responding to the final controller's corrections after the IP's verbal prompts. Heading corrections reached 10 degrees and altitude until on final 300 feet, recognized and corrected with delay but without IP control intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness of the response to controller corrections is expected to improve.

SP executed the GCA approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual and Local Area Procedures without verbal prompting from the IP. Minor errors of up to 8 degrees of heading and 220 feet of altitude until on final were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, and airspeed stayed within 15 knots above final approach speed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the PAR final accurately and promptly, applying azimuth and elevation corrections as issued by the final controller. Altitude until on final was held within 150 feet, heading within 5 degrees, airspeed within +10/-5 knots, and the aircraft stayed only slightly above or slightly below the glide path to decision height. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the GCA approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual, MAIP and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 with negligible deviations in heading, altitude and airspeed. Glide path was maintained with inputs so small that no repeat corrections were required from the final controller, and the approach was flown to decision height with no IP comment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to over-controlling in response to the final controller's azimuth corrections, did not stabilize the heading on the PAR final, with the result that heading excursions exceeded 10 degrees either side of the corrected value and the IP had to direct the roll-out and fly part of the final. Further practice of small, held heading corrections on GCA final is required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the landing configuration before intercepting the glide path, with the result that airspeed fell more than 10 knots below final approach speed and altitude until on final exceeded 300 feet from the assigned value. The IP directed the corrections and took the controls before decision height.

SP, due to a delayed correction technique after each controller call, did not hold the assigned altitude until on final, with the result of a 300 feet deviation that was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. The error was recognized and corrected with delay, without IP control intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not apply the final controller's azimuth corrections as issued, with the result that heading reached 10 degrees from the corrected value before the IP's verbal prompt. Recognition and correction were delayed, but no IP control input was required.

SP executed the GCA approach within the desired standards and without IP intervention. Heading and altitude deviations twice reached 8 degrees and 220 feet until on final, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter instrument cross-check on final is expected to reduce the size of these corrections.

SP flew the PAR approach accurately and promptly IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual and Local Area Procedures. Heading was held within 5 degrees of the corrected value, altitude until on final within 150 feet, airspeed within +10/-5 knots, and glide path deviations remained slightly above or slightly below to decision height. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the GCA approach with negligible deviations in heading, altitude until on final and airspeed, and with immediate, correctly sized responses to every controller correction. Glide path was maintained with no repeat calls from the final controller, and the approach was continued to decision height with no IP comment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power and pitch technique for glide path capture, did not arrest the sink rate at the final controller's below glide path calls, with the result that the aircraft went more than 150 feet low in the last part of the final and the IP took the controls. Further practice of glide path control on PAR final is required.

SP, due to continuation of the approach after the parameters had already been exceeded, did not initiate the missed approach when the deviations could no longer be corrected, with the result that airspeed remained more than 20 knots above final approach speed and the IP directed and executed the go-around. Recognition of the undesired aircraft state came only after IP input.

SP, due to a coarse power technique after configuring, did not hold final approach speed on the PAR final, with the result of a 20 knots excess that was reduced only after the IP's verbal prompt. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay, without IP control intervention.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the controller's corrections, did not maintain the assigned altitude until on final, with the result of a 300 feet deviation that was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt. The correction was then applied late, with no IP control input.

SP, due to a slightly delayed roll-out on the azimuth corrections, did not hold the corrected heading on final, with the result of deviations up to 8 degrees, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. The approach was completed to decision height IAW Local Area Procedures.

SP, due to divided attention between the approach checklist and the final controller's transmissions, did not maintain the assigned altitude until on final, with the result of a 220 feet deviation and a momentary excursion 200 feet high on the glide path. Both errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP executed the GCA approach accurately, holding heading within 5 degrees, altitude until on final within 150 feet and airspeed within +10/-5 knots. Elevation corrections were of the correct size but were applied slightly late twice in the last part of the final, so the parameters were regained near the edge of the desired values. Marginal performance for the Training Section - anticipation of the final controller's elevation corrections is expected to improve.

SP executed the GCA approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual, MAIP and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 with negligible deviations in heading, altitude and airspeed. Every azimuth and elevation correction was applied immediately and in the correct amount, and the aircraft was flown to decision height without a single repeat call from the final controller. Above end of block MIF achieved.
